question.text: Mr. Ravi Subramanian's Cat I Infra AIF 'Ganga Infra Yield Fund' is evaluating two opportunities: (i) acquiring an operating highway toll concession and (ii) funding a greenfield solar farm. Which characterisation aligns with Chapter 9's distinction?

answer.text: Both are brownfield since both are infra.
Both are greenfield since both require active management.
(i) is greenfield and (ii) is brownfield — the mapping is inverted.
(i) is brownfield/operating-asset — lower construction risk, stable cash flows; (ii) is greenfield — construction risk, delayed cash flows, higher expected return.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 groups infra investments into operating assets, greenfield, and brownfield. Operating-asset (brownfield in common usage) investments target already-built assets with stable cash flows (toll concessions, REIT units). Greenfield means building from scratch — construction risk, ramp-up risk, higher IRR expectation. The Trap: Options A, C, D conflate or invert the terms. In project-finance parlance, 'operating'/brownfield = existing asset; greenfield = new build. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A tests infra classification at distributor level. XV uses it in infra equity research. XIX-C covered this. Manager's Pro-Tip: When the IC debates greenfield vs brownfield, insist on separate IRR hurdles — 14% for operating/brownfield, 18%+ for greenfield with construction risk. Blending hurdles hides the construction-risk premium and distorts portfolio-level risk-adjusted returns.
